content.text: Characterized by the development of multiple symptoms after exposure to 1+ traumatic events (intrusive sxs, avoidance, negative alterations in thoughts & mood, increased arousal)
TRAUMA OCCURRED AT ANY TIME IN PAST, SXS LAST ≥1MO
(greater risk of exposure to traumatic events e.g., rape)
•80% comorbidity w/ MDD, bipolar, anxiety, substance use disorder
: directly experienced, witnessed in person, learning trauma occurred to family/friend, repeated/extreme exposure to aversive details of trauma
: memories, dreams, flashbacks, internal/external cues that results in psychological/physiological distress/reactions
: memories/thoughts/feelings, external reminders (people, places, conversations, situations, etc.)

: memory loss, persistent negative beliefs/expectations of oneself/others/the world, distorted cognitions about cause/consequence of trauma leadings to blaming of self/others, persistent negative emotional state (fear, horror, anger, guilt, shame), diminished interest/participation in significant activities, feelings of detachment/estrangement, inability to experience positive emotions
: irritable/angry outbursts, reckless/self-destructive, hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, concentration problems, sleep disturbance
•may augment w/ atypical AP in severe cases
Diagnosed in patients who experience a major traumatic event & suffer from similar symptoms at PTSD, but for a shorter duration
: directly experienced, witnessed in person, learning trauma occurred to family/friend, repeated/extreme exposure to aversive details of trauma
9+ SXS FROM ANY OF THE 5 CATEGORIES
: memories, dreams, flashbacks, psychological distress/physiological reactions
: memories/thoughts/feelings, external reminders (people, places, conversations, situations, etc.)
: sleep disturbance, irritable/angry outburst, hypervigilance, concentration problems, exaggerated startle response
Occur when behavioral or emotional symptoms develop after a non-life-threatening, stressful life event (divorce, death of loved one, fired)
May occur at any age, triggered by psychosocial factors
to the severity or intensity of stressor
in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning
Once stressor &/or its consequences have terminated,
: based on predominance of either depressed mood, anxiety, mixed anxiety/depression, conduct disturbance (e.g., aggression), or mixed disturbances of emotions/conduct
: pharmacotherapy to target symptoms (insomnia, anxiety, depression)
